extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers (postdocs) and their institutions applying for NIH K99/R00 career development awards
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an NIH K99/R00 Career Development (K) application and meeting the review standards used by NIH peer reviewers to assess candidate potential, career development plan, research plan, mentorship, institutional commitment, and required compliance elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effort requirements (K99 and R00 phases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must devote no less than 75% (no less than 50% for surgical specialties) of full-time, 12-month professional effort to research (i.e., full-time for 9 person-months). For R00 phase, the required 9 person-months of research effort need not be devoted exclusively to the R00-supported research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physician-scientists in surgical specialties may request a minimum of 50% effort. Candidates with VA appointments may not consider part of the VA effort toward satisfying the full time requirement at the applicant institution. After award receipt, adjustments to required level of effort may be made in certain circumstances (see NOT-OD-18-156 and NIH Grants Policy Statement Section 12.3.6.4). Institutions must provide assurance that the candidate will be able to devote the minimum person-months during the K99 phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess the likelihood that the proposed career development and research plan will enhance the candidate's potential for a productive, independent scientific research career in a health-related field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers take into consideration the scored criteria (Candidate; Career Development Plan; Research Plan; Mentors; Environment & Institutional Commitment) when determining the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the candidate’s potential to become an independent investigator based on prior research/training, publication record, referees' evaluations, and the quality and originality of prior and current research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider years of postdoctoral research experience, record of research productivity (including quality of peer-reviewed publications), quality of pre- and postdoctoral training, and whether it is reasonable to expect the candidate can achieve an independent, tenure-track (or equivalent) position within the time requested for the K99 phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan / Career Goals and Objectives (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the content and duration of the proposed career development components and their appropriateness to the candidate's stage and goals, and the plan's likely contribution to transition to independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the plan augments prior training, contributes substantially to scientific/professional development, includes adequate plans for evaluating progress and transition milestones, has an appropriate timeline for transition, and (if applicable) whether clinical trial experience contributes to career development. Candidates must justify need for mentored K99 support and provide a timeline with milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The research plan must span both K99 and R00 phases and be described sufficiently for reviewers to evaluate the merit of each phase, including significance, innovation, and approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should: clearly indicate research for each phase; describe what will be accomplished in the mentored phase to enable launch of an independent program; provide detailed rationale, experimental approach, expected/alternative outcomes; address rigor and plans to address weaknesses in prior research; present strategies to ensure robust/unbiased approaches and to address relevant biological variables (e.g., sex); describe relationship to mentor's work and how the candidate will gain independence; and, for R00, provide sufficient detail and evidence of long-term viability. If clinical trial experience is proposed, describe its relationship to the career development and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor(s), Co-Mentor(s), Consultant(s), Collaborator(s) (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the mentors' qualifications, mentoring track record, appropriateness of mentorship and supervision, and commitment to the applicant's career development and transition to independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submission the candidate must identify a mentor who is an active investigator committed to direct supervision and career development. Mentor(s) must document sufficient research support/facilities. Mentoring teams are encouraged; one individual must be designated primary mentor. If the primary mentor has limited training experience, include a co-mentor with a strong track record. Mentor statements must include: (1) research qualifications and prior supervisory experience; (2) plan describing supervision/mentoring during K99 including fostering independence; (3) description of planned research training and coursework; (4) plan for transitioning to independence and how mentor will help; (5) statement identifying research components the K99 applicant may take to the R00; and (6) when appropriate, affirmation of resources/reagents that can be taken to R00. Mentor should state ability to cover costs beyond award or identify other sources. Primary mentor must agree to provide annual evaluations and assist in job search/transition. For clinical-trial-related career development, mentor/co-mentor must document leadership and appropriate expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment & Institutional Commitment to the Candidate (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the sponsoring institution's research environment, resources, and commitment to developing the candidate into an independent investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsoring institution must document a strong, well-established research and career development program related to the candidate’s area, provide assurance the candidate can devote minimum person-months (9 person-months/75% effort), that research facilities, resources, training opportunities and collaborating faculty will be available, and that appropriate time/support for mentor(s) will be provided during the K99. For non-U.S. citizens, include visa status assurance. For individuals in postdoctoral roles with other titles, provide evidence of eligibility for K99/R00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must include a plan to fulfill NIH requirements for instruction in RCR and reviewers will evaluate adequacy relative to candidate's experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate five required components: (1) Format (face-to-face lectures, coursework, and/or real-time discussion groups; online-only is not acceptable); (2) Subject Matter (e.g., conflict of interest, authorship, data management, human subjects and animal use, lab safety, research misconduct, research ethics); (3) Faculty Participation (role of mentors and faculty); (4) Duration (at least eight contact hours required); and (5) Frequency (instruction must occur during each career stage and at least once every four years). Plans/past record will be rated ACCEPTABLE or UNACCEPTABLE and the summary statement will provide the committee consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (additional review criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: For NIH-defined human subjects research (non-exempt), reviewers evaluate justification for involving human subjects and proposed protections from research risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation is according to five review criteria: (1) risk to subjects; (2) adequacy of protection against risks; (3) potential benefits to subjects and others; (4) importance of knowledge to be gained; and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials. For exempt research, reviewers evaluate justification for exemption, human subjects involvement and characteristics, and sources of materials. Follow Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion (women, minorities, ages)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the project involves human subjects/clinical research, reviewers evaluate plans for inclusion or justified exclusion of individuals on the basis of sex, race, ethnicity, and of all ages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers determine whether inclusion/exclusion plans are scientifically justified relative to the study goals and research strategy. Refer to NIH Guidelines for Inclusion in Clinical Research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals (additional review criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: When live vertebrate animals are involved, reviewers evaluate the description and justification of animal use and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review considers: (1) complete description of proposed procedures including species, strains, ages, sex, and total numbers; (2) justification that species is appropriate and alternatives not suitable; (3) interventions (analgesia, anesthesia, sedation, palliative care, humane endpoints) to limit pain/distress. Methods of euthanasia must be justified if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines and other guidance uses the Vertebrate Animals Worksheet for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether proposed materials or procedures pose hazards to personnel or the environment, and whether adequate protections are proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers examine descriptions of hazardous agents/procedures and biosafety plans to determine if protections are sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess plans for use of Select Agent(s) including registration, monitoring, and biosafety/biocontainment/security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation includes (1) the Select Agent(s) to be used; (2) registration status of entities where agents will be used; (3) procedures to monitor possession/use/transfer; and (4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: For projects involving key biological/chemical resources, reviewers comment on plans to identify and ensure the validity of those resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide brief plans to authenticate reagents, cell lines, antibodies, etc.; reviewers will comment on adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers consider whether the budget and requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable relative to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the K99 phase provide itemized budgets for each budget period. For the R00 phase a total requested amount per period is acceptable in initial application, with specific form-entry requirements (Budget Type, start/end dates, PD/PI entry with appropriate level of effort and $0 requested salary/fringe, Section F: Other Direct Costs line item titled 'R00 Independent Phase' with total request up to $249,000). At transition, R00 applicant institution will submit a detailed budget reflecting direct and indirect costs at the R00 institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support, Collaborators, Contributors, Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Signed statements from collaborators/consultants confirming participation and describing specific roles must be provided; advisory committee members (if applicable) must provide signed statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborators/consultants (unless also senior/key personnel) do not need to provide biosketches. Statements should document appropriate expertise and clearly describe roles. Applications lacking required reference letters will not be reviewed; reference letters are submitted separately through eRA Commons 'Submit Referee Information'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Content & Form Compliance (How to Apply instructions, page limits, forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must follow instructions in the How to Apply - Application Guide and conform to page limits and form requirements; non-compliant applications may be delayed or not accepted for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ASSIST or institutional system-to-system if applicable. Follow all specific form instructions (SF424(R&R) cover, PHS 398 forms, Project/Performance Sites, Senior/Key Person Profile Expanded, R&R Budget, PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information, PHS Assignment Request Form). All page limitations in the How to Apply and Table of Page Limits must be followed. Limited items are allowed in the Appendix; follow Appendix instructions. Applications will be evaluated for completeness/compliance upon receipt; incomplete/non-compliant applications will not be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing Plan (DMSP)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants planning research that results in generation of scientific data must include a Data Management and Sharing Plan attached in the Other Plan(s) attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective for due dates on/after Jan 25, 2023, the DMSP is to be attached in the Other Plan(s) section of FORMS-H packages; all applications must address DMSP regardless of direct cost requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Letters submission timing and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must follow the How to Apply Guide regarding the time period when reference letters will be accepted; reference letters are submitted directly through eRA Commons rather than Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications lacking the appropriate required reference letters will not be reviewed. This submission is a separate process from submitting the application electronically; use the eRA Commons 'Submit Referee Information' link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations and Unique Entity Identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant organizations must have required registrations and provide the same unique entity identifier across systems (eRA Commons profile, SAM, Grants.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete required registrations (unique entity identifier, active SAM registration, NCAGE if applicable, eRA Commons, Grants.gov) before application due date. PD(s)/PIs must include their eRA Commons ID in the Credential field of the Senior/Key Person Profile form. Failure to register or include a valid Commons ID will prevent successful submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process, dates, and timely corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted electronically via Grants.gov using ASSIST or other allowed systems, and applicants must track status in eRA Commons; errors identified by NIH/Grants.gov must be corrected before the due date/time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to submit early to allow corrections. If a Changed/Corrected application is submitted after the deadline it will be considered late. When a submission date falls on a weekend or Federal holiday the deadline automatically extends to next business day. Applicants are responsible for viewing their application in eRA Commons before the due date to ensure an accurate submission. For system issues beyond control, follow 'Dealing with System Issues' guidance and contact Application Submission Contacts in Section VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission materials policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must follow the NIH policy for post-submission materials; any additional instructions here are in addition to the policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit materials post-review unless allowed by policy; follow the provided policy link and NOFO-specific additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmissions and Revisions (review considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmissions are evaluated as presented, taking into consideration responses to previous review comments. Revisions are evaluated for appropriateness of proposed expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Resubmissions, reviewers consider the applicant's responses to prior scientific review group comments and changes made. For Revisions, consider whether expansion of scope is appropriate and whether responses to prior critiques are adequate and substantive changes are evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (including model organisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether resource sharing plans (e.g., Sharing Model Organisms) or rationale for not sharing are reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear Resource Sharing Plans or justification for not sharing. Reviewers will comment but these items are not scored separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and review outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are evaluated for scientific and technical merit by Scientific Review Group(s); generally only top half may be discussed and assigned an overall impact score; applicants will receive a written critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment to an NIH Institute/Center is based on PHS referral guidelines. Applications compete for funds with other recommended applications. The review follows NIH peer review policies and practices.
